pies.title: Pies
pies.subtitle: Target allocations for your portfolio: set a weight per slice and see how far your holdings have drifted.

empty.title: No pies yet
empty.description: A pie splits your portfolio into slices, each a category, a subcategory or specific holdings, with a target weight. Fiscalis then shows how far your actual allocation drifts from it.

card.noHoldings: None of your holdings match this pie's slices yet.
card.threshold: Slices more than {threshold} percentage points off target need rebalancing.
card.missingHoldings: {count, plural, one {# holding} other {# holdings}} no longer in your portfolio

delete.title: Delete this pie?
delete.description: “{name}” and its target weights will be deleted. Your holdings are not affected.

editor.description: Give each slice a target weight. The weights must add up to 100%.
editor.name: Name
editor.noHoldings: You have no holdings to choose from yet.
editor.label: Label
editor.totalOff: Total: {total}%. The weights must add up to 100%.

goals.title: Goals
goals.subtitle: Things you want to buy, unlocked by rules you set. Only new money and activity after a goal starts count toward it.
goals.debt: {pool} owes {amount} from a goal bought before it was earned. New progress repays this first, before any goal can use it.
goals.estimated: {count, plural, one {On # day} other {On # days}}, the money moved into investments had to be estimated, so some figures are approximate.

empty.title: No goals yet
empty.description: Give a goal a price and a rule, for example: invest ten times the price before you book the trip.

delete.title: Delete this goal?
delete.description: {name} and its progress will be deleted. This can't be undone.

card.boughtEarlyHint: The rule wasn't met yet, so the shortfall became debt.
card.ruleChanges: {count, plural, one {The rule was changed once} other {The rule was changed # times}}, most recently on {date}.

invested.multiple: Invest {multiple}× the price in new money

gains.multiple: Gains of {multiple}× the price on your investments

rule.cooldown: Wait {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}

streak.week: {tracker}: {perPeriod} times a week for {periods, plural, one {# week} other {# weeks}} in a row
streak.month: {tracker}: {perPeriod} times a month for {periods, plural, one {# month} other {# months}} in a row

editor.description: Set what you want to buy and the rule that unlocks it. Only new money and activity from today on count.
editor.name: Name
editor.startDateHint: While you set up your first goals you can date one back to when you really started working toward it. Only money and activity from that day on count.
editor.ruleHint: Fiscalis tracks money, gains, net worth and waiting periods itself. Counts, streaks, checklists and measurements are what you log.
editor.nestedRule: This rule has groups inside groups, which the builder can't show. Saving keeps it as it is.
editor.atLeastCount: How many checks must be met
editor.invalid: Check the highlighted values: every target must be above zero.
editor.noTrackers: Add a tracker of this kind below the goals first.

purchase.title: Mark {name} as bought
purchase.description: Enter what you actually paid. The rule is checked again at that price.
purchase.earned: Your rule is met at {price}. Buying it uses:
purchase.early: Your rule isn't met at {price} yet. You can still mark it as bought: what's missing becomes debt that new progress repays first. Buying it uses:
purchase.toastEarly: {name} marked as bought before it was earned

trackers.title: Trackers
trackers.description: Things you log yourself for your goals, like workouts or a 10 km time. Fiscalis trusts these entries.
trackers.name: Tracker name
